clue.text: Bishop to survive explosion

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to last is to survive or endure

explanation.surface: A churchman somehow lives through a bomb going off.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is the rush of air and noise from a detonation, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Italian engineer having problem with mindset? Not half

indicators.note: only half of the preceding word survives, so the back half is cut away

parts.note: a bug is a fault or problem
an attitude is a settled way of thinking

explanation.surface: Some engineer from Italy seems to have trouble with his way of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps only the first half of the word before it; the question mark admits mindset is a loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettore Bugatti was the Italian-born car designer who founded the famous marque of racing and luxury cars.

clue.text: A love for Ancient Rome reflected peculiar charm

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the Latin word is read the other way

parts.note: amor is the Latin word for love, the word Ancient Rome would use

explanation.surface: A passion for classical Rome mirrors some special allure.
explanation.walkthrough: Rome tempts the solver to lift its Italian name directly, but it only says the love word is Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive scent, a characteristic quality that charms or attracts, hence a peculiar (particular) charm.

clue.text: Support hospital governance arrangements later time will abandon

indicators.note: the later of two time abbreviations walks out, leaving the word one letter shorter

parts.note: NHS hospitals in England are run by trusts
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Backing for new hospital management schemes that will drop a time limit later.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUSTS contains two Ts; it is the second, the later one, that goes. NHS trusts are the bodies that run British hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a framework or bandage that bears weight or holds something up, so it is a support.

clue.text: Description of special treatment favoured by Yorkshire resort

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town on the Yorkshire coast
a pet project or pet theory is a favoured one

explanation.surface: A VIP welcome said to be preferred by a northern seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favoured by' places the favoured word beside the resort, coming after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is the idiom for giving a guest lavish, ceremonial treatment.

clue.text: Gain power and more money in review

parts.note: to reap is to gain the rewards
P is the physics symbol for power
a raise is an increase in pay; 'and' just joins it on

explanation.surface: An employee secures authority and a pay rise during an appraisal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess again, the verb sense of review.

clue.text: Avoid 'upper-class' in description of current King

indicators.note: one item sits inside another, so the posh letter goes within the electrical term

parts.note: DC, direct current, describes a kind of current
U is the old label for upper-class usage
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Steer clear of calling the present monarch posh.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside DC, and K follows. 'Current King' looks like a reference to the reigning monarch, but current is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or evade it, as you duck a blow.

clue.text: My breeding activity's frowned upon, possibly producing ultra-deer?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the following word could be one of several arrangements

parts.note: a nonsense compound whose letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: A disapproved-of stag asks whether its love life might create some super-deer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the voice of the answer: someone whose sexual activity outside marriage is disapproved of.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer commits adultery, sexual relations outside marriage, which society traditionally frowns upon.

clue.text: Audit top person's initially scuppered

indicators.note: a scuppered ship is wrecked, so these letters are wrecked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of person

explanation.surface: An audit brings down the boss in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuppered' does double duty here: it shuffles the letters and is also the meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To put paid to something is to end or ruin it decisively, just as scuppering a plan wrecks it.

clue.text: Nasty sort collaring navy over threat to shipping?

indicators.note: to collar someone is to grab them round the neck, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a toad is a loathsome person
RN is the Royal Navy
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A villain seizes the fleet, menacing the ships.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a whirlwind is only one example of danger at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating storm, and a waterspout version is a hazard to vessels at sea.

clue.text: Group of stars round California primarily having renown in Hollywood

parts.note: globular means spherical

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the state counts

parts.note: the first letter of California
lustre, meaning glory, in its American spelling

explanation.surface: A clique of film stars in California enjoys fame in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' looks like celebrities; it is astronomical. Hollywood signals the US spelling LUSTER rather than LUSTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A globular cluster is a dense spherical swarm of hundreds of thousands of old stars orbiting a galaxy.

clue.text: Tutor skipping one month to see part of church

indicators.note: skipping means leaving something out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to tutor someone is to train them
I is the Roman numeral one
SEPT is the abbreviation for September

explanation.surface: A teacher misses a month of lessons to visit a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, crossing the nave at right angles.

clue.text: Station with rodent penetrating layers

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so the animal goes into the other piece

parts.note: STA is a standard abbreviation for station
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A railway station overrun by rats burrowing into the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata is the plural of stratum, a layer of rock or of society.

clue.text: Less happy about cat, say, climbing large item in tool shed?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the comparative word goes around the rest

parts.note: sadder means less happy
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means moving upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a cat is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that the cat has climbed onto a big object in the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat climbing is the reversal signal; a cat clambering up a ladder also suits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a folding portable ladder, the sort of thing typically kept in a garden shed.

clue.text: Frenchmen, I allow, will pursue one person new to the country?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MM abbreviates messieurs, the French for gentlemen
I grant means I allow or concede

explanation.surface: A French group agrees to follow a newcomer to the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will pursue' means the first two parts come after I; the order is one, then the Frenchmen, then I allow.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant has come from abroad to settle, so is a new arrival in the country; the question mark covers a loose definition.

clue.text: Way of working to exploit actor's role turning up in play-within-a-play

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
to use someone is to exploit them

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up flips the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A method for exploiting a role that turns up in a play staged within a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is from Hamlet, not Agatha Christie's long-running play of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mousetrap is the name Hamlet gives the play staged before Claudius to catch the king's conscience.

clue.text: Welsh hero's fierce expression about death

indicators.note: about means around, so the angry look surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a glower is an angry scowl
death is one's end

explanation.surface: A national champion of Wales scowls at the thought of dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes the 's, read as 'is': the Welsh hero is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndwr, anglicised as Glendower, led the Welsh revolt against English rule around 1400 and is a national hero.

clue.text: Recalled row about detective's call

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned word goes around the officer
recalled is taken as called back, so the word runs in the backward direction

parts.note: to row is to use an oar; the noun stands for the rowing
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: An argument remembered over a detective's phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means oar; DI then goes inside the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio someone is to call them by wireless transmission, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stimulate American to import eggs? On the contrary

indicators.text: to import eggs? On the contrary
indicators.note: importing means taking inside, and the reversal phrase swaps which piece is inside which

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
US abbreviates American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: Shake up a US citizen into bringing in eggs from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the instruction: the eggs take in the American, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to stir up or wake someone, a synonym for stimulate.

clue.text: Things improvised to restrict Post Office swindles

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: riffs are improvised musical phrases
PO is Post Office

explanation.surface: Ad-hoc measures limiting the Post Office lead to fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the British Post Office accounting scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip-offs are frauds or overcharges, the informal noun for swindles.

clue.text: Power seen in sun over a cataclysmic stellar explosion

indicators.note: a cataclysm is a violent upheaval, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Energy in the sun spills over into a violent explosion of a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is the enormous explosion of a dying star, briefly outshining a whole galaxy.

clue.text: One engaged in breaking down or treating breakdowns

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who examines things by separating them into parts
second meaning: a psychoanalyst who treats people suffering mental collapse

explanation.walkthrough: Breaking down plays on two senses: dissecting data, and nervous collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a data or chemical examiner and, informally, a psychotherapist who treats patients.

clue.text: Work involving payments recalled as sham

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so everything runs backwards
involving means wrapping around, so the work surrounds the payments

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
dues are payments owed

explanation.surface: A project with fees later withdrawn as fraudulent.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first, and then the whole combination reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means false or pretended, as an adjective synonym of sham.

clue.text: A doctor is among company backing support for Asian country

indicators.note: being among something means sitting in its midst, so the doctor phrase goes inside

parts.note: CO abbreviates company
taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: backing is read as going backwards, so the help word runs right to left

parts.note: aid is support

explanation.surface: A medic joins a firm that backs relief for a country in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the standard crossword doctor alongside DR and MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a nation in South-East Asia, bordering Thailand, Laos and Vietnam.

clue.text: Standard article, and second, written in pen

indicators.note: what is written in something is set inside it

parts.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
a is the indefinite article; 'and' joins it to the next
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An ordinary piece of writing with a follow-up done in ink.
explanation.walkthrough: A and S go inside BIC, the ballpoint pen brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and standard both describe the plain, default version of something, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Tense, absorbed in endless waiting for fourth in line?

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken inside something else
endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a delay is a period of waiting
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone tensely waits as fourth in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: DELAY loses its last letter to DELA, and T goes inside. The line is the NATO phonetic alphabet (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta), not a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek and the phonetic alphabets, the code word for D.

clue.text: God is loving, ignoring Catholic

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: someone who is loving cares
C is the abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: A deity is loving, but pays no heed to Catholics.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C from CARES to leave ARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, the counterpart of the Roman Mars.

clue.text: Encourage toil and all but destroy relaxation? Many reports shedding light here

indicators.note: all but means nearly everything, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to fire someone up is to encourage them
toil is work
slang: to diss or destroy someone is to tear them apart in words
play is recreation, relaxation

explanation.surface: A slave-driver urges hard work and nearly abolishes leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: DISS loses its last letter to DIS. The reports are bangs, not documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireworks show is full of loud reports (bangs) while rockets light up the sky.

clue.text: Country in South America having little hesitation getting control of system

definitions.note: the answer is the account or user that holds such control

parts.note: S abbreviates south

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the nation goes within the abbreviation

parts.note: US is the United States of America
Peru is a country
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A South American nation hesitates briefly before taking over the system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' looks like one place but splits into two abbreviations, with the country set inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A superuser is the computing account with unrestricted administrative privileges, i.e. full command over the system.

clue.text: What angler will do, catching nothing in seaside area

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the empty letter is taken in

parts.note: an angler casts a line
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A fisherman casts but catches nothing at the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the land bordering the sea, the area where the seaside lies.
